desc:
There are n integer variables x0 .. xn-1. You are given a list of constraints, each written as [a, op, b]:

  • op = 0 means xa = xb (equal)
  • op = 1 means xa ≠ xb (different)

Return true if some assignment of integers to the variables satisfies all constraints at the same time, otherwise false. Note that a and b may be the same variable.

n = 4, equations = [[0,0,1],[1,0,2],[2,1,3]]   -> true   (x0=x1=x2, x3 different)
n = 3, equations = [[0,0,1],[1,0,2],[0,1,2]]   -> false  (x0=x1=x2 but x0 != x2)
n = 2, equations = [[1,1,1]]                    -> false  (x1 != x1)
constraints: equations[i] = [a, op, b] with 0 ≤ a, b < n and op in {0, 1}
hints: Equality is transitive: if x0 = x1 and x1 = x2 then x0 = x2. Which data structure keeps groups of variables that must be equal?
First put every pair from an equality constraint into the same group. The groups can then take pairwise different values if they want to.
After all equalities are processed, check every != constraint: it is violated exactly when both variables ended up in the same group (including a == b).
editorial: Because there are infinitely many integers, any two groups that are not forced to be equal can simply be given different values. So the only way to fail is a != constraint between two variables that equality constraints force to be the same.

Run union-find over all constraints with op = 0. Then scan the constraints with op = 1 and return false if find(a) == find(b). The order of the input does not matter, but the two passes do: all equalities must be merged before any inequality is judged. Time O((n + m) α(n)), space O(n).
